(2026)", "metaDescription": "Kodely vs Webflow compared honestly: chat-based AI code generation vs visual canvas editing, pricing, code ownership, hosting, CMS, and e-commerce.", "targetKeyword": "kodely vs webflow", "category": "Comparisons", "bodyHtml": "

TL;DR verdict

Kodely and Webflow solve different problems. Kodely is a chat-based tool that generates a real React and TypeScript codebase from a plain-English description and publishes it free on a kodely.site subdomain. Webflow is a visual, drag-and-drop canvas for designers that outputs real HTML and CSS, with a mature CMS, e-commerce, and custom domains. If you want to describe a site and get a working app live in minutes with no design-tool learning curve, Kodely wins. If you need pixel-level visual control, a content management system, or an online store, Webflow is the more complete tool today.

Pricing and the credit model

Kodely runs on credits tied to real AI cost, not a seat-based subscription. Every new account gets 750 credits free, no credit card required. A first build typically costs roughly 100 to 150 credits, and a follow-up change in chat usually costs about the same. If a generation fails to compile, Kodely runs one automatic repair attempt and you are never charged for a failed build. When you need more credits, top-ups are $9 for 500 credits, $40 for 2,500 credits (the most popular option), or $90 for 6,000 credits, and credits never expire. Webflow instead uses recurring site and workspace plans, typically billed monthly or annually, with separate tiers once you need CMS content limits or e-commerce. That model makes sense if you are running an ongoing content-heavy site, but it means you pay every month whether you touch the site or not. Kodely's model is closer to metered usage: you pay for what you actually build.

Do you own the code?

This is where the two tools diverge philosophically. Every Kodely project starts from a real foundation codebase with hand-built UI primitives (Button, Card, Section, Nav) and every change you request in chat edits real .tsx component files, not a template swap. You can open the code view in-app and see and copy the actual generated source at any time. What Kodely does not yet offer is a full project export or zip download, so today the code lives inside Kodely until that export ships. Webflow also renders genuine HTML and CSS rather than a black-box template, and offers code export on eligible plans, which gives you more portability than Kodely currently does. If owning a fully exportable codebase on day one matters most to you, that is a real point in Webflow's favor right now.

Hosting and going live

Kodely's publish step is free and instant: one click puts your project live on a real public URL at yourname.kodely.site, with no separate hosting purchase, no server setup, and every publish scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live. The tradeoff is that Kodely does not support custom domains yet, so you cannot point yourdomain.com at a Kodely site today. Webflow includes hosting in its plans too, but it also supports connecting your own custom domain, which matters for any business that wants a branded URL rather than a subdomain.

Backend, CMS, and e-commerce depth

Kodely generates a frontend application only. There is no backend, database, authentication, or payment processing generation, and no built-in CMS for managing blog posts or dynamic content. Webflow has spent years building out a genuinely mature CMS and a full e-commerce system, including product catalogs, cart, and checkout. If your project needs dynamic content editors for non-technical teammates, or you are selling products online, Webflow is simply more built out today.

Visual control: chat vs canvas

Kodely has no click-to-edit visual editor. You describe what you want changed in chat, watch the live preview update as the real compiled app, and every successful generation becomes a free checkpoint you can roll back to. That is fast, but it means you cannot nudge a single element five pixels to the left by hand. Webflow's canvas is built exactly for that kind of fine-grained visual control, which is why it remains the standard for designers who need precision.

Best for: the honest verdict

Choose Kodely if you want to go from an idea to a live, real-code site in minutes without learning a design tool, and you are comfortable iterating by describing changes rather than dragging elements. It is a strong fit for landing pages, marketing sites, prototypes, and indie projects where speed and a clean codebase matter more than pixel precision. Choose Webflow if you are a design-focused agency or team that needs a CMS, e-commerce, custom domains, or exact visual control today. Webflow is the more complete, mature product for that work right now, and Kodely does not pretend otherwise.

FAQ

Is Kodely open source or self-hostable?

No. Kodely is a hosted product; there is no self-hosting option.

Can I download or export my Kodely project?

Not yet. You can view and copy the generated source files in-app, but there is no zip or full-project download at this time.

Does Kodely support custom domains?

Not yet. Published sites are live on a free yourname.kodely.site subdomain only.

Does Kodely have a free trial?

Yes. Every new account gets 750 credits free with no credit card required.

Does Kodely include a CMS or e-commerce like Webflow?

No. Kodely currently generates frontend applications only, with no backend, database, CMS, or payment processing.

If speed and a real codebase matter more than pixel-level control right now, start building free on Kodely and see a live site in minutes.
